description: Set who may read a session: private (its authors only), or team (every author in your tenant; the default). To let someone outside the tenant read it, use share_link. Only the session's author or an admin token may set it; the latest setting wins and applies to every read at once.

request_key.description: Optional idempotency key; a retry with the same key changes nothing.

session_id.description: A session id as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return it (session:...).

name: set_visibility

description: Request that a session be deleted: from the moment this returns no read (search_sessions, open, list_sessions, file_attention) shows it to anyone. The request is recorded and cannot be undone; the stored data is not physically removed. Only the session's author or an admin token may request it.

request_key.description: Optional idempotency key; defaults to one per session.

session_id.description: A session id as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return it (session:...).

name: delete_session

description: Judge a session or one span of it: append a score (number), a label or a text note, tagged with who or what made the judgment (human, scorer or ci). Annotations are append-only records, never overwritten; the author is your token's, not an argument. Needs a token with the annotate scope and a session you may open. The annotation shows in get_trace after the next converge (a few seconds). A retry with the same request_id, or with the same content when none is given, changes nothing.

label.description: A short categorical value such as pass or regression.

name.description: What is judged, such as correctness or tests_passed.

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key; defaults to a hash of the annotation without its time.

session_id.description: A session id as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return it (session:...).

source.description: Who judged: human, scorer (an automatic grader) or ci.

span_id.description: A span id from get_trace; omit to judge the whole session.

name: annotate

description: Return a session's span tree: invoke_agent, turn, chat (model call) and execute_tool spans nested under their parents, with start, end, status, model, token counts and cost where the source reports it, session totals, and the annotations on the session and on each span. The text is the same tree indented one level per depth.

include_annotations.description: Attach the session's annotations; false returns the spans alone.

session_id.description: A session id as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return it (session:...).

name: get_trace

description: Ask one read-only question over your tenant's sessions in mnemonic's query language: clauses, not SQL. Clauses, separated by | or newlines, each at most once: from: one relation (required); filter: a predicate; select: expressions or * for rows, or dimensions: and measures: for groups; sort: keys with asc or desc; limit: n. Example: from: events | filter: harness = 'codex' and tool_phase = 'request' | dimensions: tool_name | measures: count() as calls | sort: calls desc | limit: 10. Relations: events (one row per event: session_id, event_ts, harness, event_kind, actor_kind, tool_name, tool_call_id, tool_phase, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, content_types, text_content, author, ...; payload_json and token_usage_json are returned only when named), sessions (session_id, first_event_time, last_event_time, total_turns, total_events, completed), turns (session_id, turn_seq, event_count, completed, terminal_uid), spans (session_id, span_id, parent_span_id, kind, name, start_time, end_time, status, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cost), annotations (annotation_id, target_session_id, target_span_id, name, value_number, value_label, value_text, source, author, ts). Operators: = != < <= > >=, and, or, not, + - * /, in ('a', 'b'), like and ilike with % and _ (pattern at most 1000 bytes), is null, is not null, column match 'words' (full text: every word present), content_types includes 'image', map['key']. A 'string' compared with a time column is read as RFC 3339 or a date. Functions: lower, length, hour, day, week, month; in measures: count(), count(x), count_distinct, sum, avg, min, max, percentile(x, 0.95). Each relation holds only rows inside from..to (events by event_ts, spans by start_time, sessions overlapping the range, annotations by ts) and only sessions you may read. from and to are required RFC 3339 timestamps at most 31 days apart. At most limit rows come back (default 100, max 10000; truncated says more existed). A query runs at most 30 s and scans every part of the store, so keep filters selective. At most 2 queries run at once; a third is refused, retry in 1 s.

query.description: One query, for example: from: sessions | filter: total_events > 50 | select: session_id, total_events | sort: total_events desc

from.description: Start of the range, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp (for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z).

to.description: End of the range, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp; at most 31 days after from.

name: query

description: Make, list or revoke links. With session_ids: a read link, one https URL anyone holding it can read those sessions at, as they are now, in a browser or with an agent, until it expires or is revoked; the answer lists each session's harness, project, start, messages and rendered size, so check what goes out before sending it. Only a session's sole author or an admin key may link it. With invite: an invite link that admits one machine, which pushes as that author into your tenant and reads what your tenant reads; inviting another author needs an admin key. With no arguments: your live links, and the key and machine that joined each invite. With revoke: end a link of either kind; a joined machine loses access at its next request. The URL is shown once and cannot be recovered.

days.description: Days until the link expires: 1 to 365; default 30 for a read link, 7 for an invite.

invite.description: The author the invited machine pushes as.

note.description: A note shown under the title of a read link.

revoke.description: The link_id of a link to revoke.

session_ids.description: Session ids as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return them (session:...), in the order the link shows them.

name: share_link
